verdict: [V] AddBootstrapPlaintexts -> Plaintext::load -> RNSPoly::loadConstant -> LimbPartition::generateLimbConstant -> Limb construction -> VectorGPU -> GPUmalloc is the exact call chain that fails, at depth=58, via heap corruption (munmap_chunk) rather than a clean CUDA error. This is the SAME code path (bootstrap-precomputation plaintext loading) that fhe_fides_gpu_multiblock_bisect_depth50_FAIL_20260724 reached and failed in cleanly (an explicit 'Cuda failure ... out of memory' at 81131/81920 MiB). Combined with the depth=64 SIGSEGV (which dies even earlier, before this stage, at only ~2GB peak) and the LARGE_DIGITS=2 side-experiment (independently broken, unrelated to this analysis), the unified picture is: every failure mode observed across depth in {50, 58, 64} and large_digits in {2, 4} traces back to GPU memory exhaustion somewhere in the rotation-key or bootstrap-precomputation-plaintext loading sequence inside LoadContext. Which specific allocation call fails first -- and whether FIDESlib's error handling at that exact call site produces a clean 'out of memory' exception or an unchecked GPUmalloc failure that corrupts the heap -- depends on the exact depth/digit/slot configuration, but the underlying cause is the same: this two-block context's total GPU memory footprint does not fit in one A100's 80GB. [U] A real fix requires reducing batch_slots and/or the rotation-key count (the two levers that directly shrink the number and size of GPU-resident keys/plaintexts), or splitting the computation across multiple GPUs. Lowering multiplicative_depth alone, or lowering large_digits alone, does not resolve it and in the large_digits=2 case introduces its own separate breakage.
